posts.heading: October 15, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 323 feeder visits, above the past week's average of 282.7, while heard detections totaled 394, below the average of 423.0. Twenty species were recorded, matching the average of 20.1, with 17 heard, 10 seen and 7 both. Tufted Titmouse led visits with 119 confident sightings and Carolina Chickadee followed with 47, while Eastern Phoebe led heard detections with 106 and Eastern Towhee had 67.

Thirteen species were recorded on all seven days, including American Crow, Blue Jay, Carolina Chickadee, Carolina Wren, Eastern Phoebe, Eastern Towhee, Gray Catbird, House Finch, Mourning Dove, Northern Cardinal, Song Sparrow, Tufted Titmouse and White-breasted Nuthatch. Canada Goose and Yellow-bellied Sapsucker were each heard once today and on no other day this week. Twelve species recorded earlier in the week were not recorded today, including American Kestrel, Cedar Waxwing, Rose-breasted Grosbeak and Pine Siskin.

The audio source was changed many times during the day, starting at 03:46 and last changed at 21:31, so each heard detection came from whichever source was active at that moment. Frequent source changes ran through the past week as well.

posts.heading: October 14, 2026
posts.text:
The day added up to 290 feeder visits and 424 detections across 20 species, with 18 heard, 14 seen, and 12 both. That is above the week's average of 258.1 visits and 414.9 detections, while the species count sat close to the average of 19.9. Visits were busier than four of the seven days before and quieter than three, with Oct 10, 11, and 12 the busiest.

Twelve species were recorded on all seven days, including this one, among them Eastern Phoebe, Carolina Chickadees, Tufted Titmice, Northern Cardinal, and Blue Jays. Eastern Phoebe led detections with 118, Carolina Chickadees followed with 61, and Tufted Titmice led confident visits with 111. Downy Woodpecker, Rose-breasted Grosbeak, and Northern Flicker were recorded earlier in the week but not today.

The audio source was switched many times through the day, between pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1), and c120, with changes logged in the morning and again in the evening. No species was seen for the first time at the station, and none was heard for the first time.

posts.heading: October 13, 2026
posts.text:
The day logged 20 species, 18 by ear and 10 by sight, with 8 seen and heard, across 209 feeder visits. That was quieter than the past-week average of 247.9 visits, while the 657 detections were well above the average of 362.0. Brown-headed Cowbird made up 281 of those detections, all logged between 10:00 and 16:00.

Twelve species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Tufted Titmouse with 80 visits and Carolina Chickadee with 38. Ten species from the past week were not recorded today, including Downy Woodpecker, American Goldfinch, and Pileated Woodpecker. The first visual record of the day was a Northern Cardinal 19 minutes before sunrise, and the last was a Tufted Titmouse 307 minutes after sunrise.

The audio source was switched many times between 07:09 and 08:06 this morning, so the early detections came from changing sources. Brown-headed Cowbird is listed as heard for the first time at this station today, and it was picked up on the audio source in use after those changes, so it is not counted as a new arrival. No species had a first confident visual record at the station today.

posts.heading: October 12, 2026
posts.text:
October 12 added up to 353 feeder visits and 23 species, above the past week's averages of 226.7 visits and 18.9 species, and the most species of any day in the past week. It was the second-busiest day for visits after Sunday's 459. Heard detections totaled 316, below the week's average of 362.3. Tufted Titmice led visits with 136, followed by Carolina Chickadees with 70, while Carolina Chickadees led detections with 63 and Eastern Towhee had 52.

Broad-winged Hawk returned after 17 days away, last recorded 2026-09-25, and Cedar Waxwing returned after 27 days, last recorded 2026-09-15; each was heard once today. Northern Cardinal was the first visual record of the day, 15 min before sunrise, and also the last, 8 min after sunset. Seven species from the past week were not recorded today: American Kestrel, Pileated Woodpecker, American Goldfinches, Eastern Bluebird, Palm Warbler, Brown Thrasher, and Pine Siskin.

The audio source was switched many times during the day, between 07:13 and 08:06 and again between 18:41 and 19:47, so the heard counts combine detections from more than one microphone.
